summary: Configured a persistent restricted SSH ingest path. As uploader on node2, submit with `ssh legacy2-ingest < batch.ndjson`. Each connection creates a separate exact-byte receipt on node1. Both nodes passed sequential reboot and recovery verification.
actions_performed: Created locked, separate uploader and ingest application identities.
Generated and retained the private ED25519 key only on node2.
Installed a root-controlled forced-command receiver on node1 with public-key-only authentication and PTY, command, forwarding, tunneling, agent, X11, and user-RC restrictions.
Verified exact-byte sample ingestion, unique receipt files, and preservation of the original sample and prior receipt.
Proved an attempted arbitrary command was not executed and a forwarding request was rejected.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot identities, configuration persistence, retained data, and end-to-end recovery.
Confirmed AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 remained installed.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated uploader key and restricted ingest identity
evidence.summary: Dedicated accounts, key fingerprint, client targeting, forced command, and effective SSH restrictions are shown.

evidence.requirement: Separate exact-byte receipts while preserving existing data
evidence.summary: The sample upload matched byte-for-byte; unique receipts were created and original sample/prior hashes remained unchanged through both restarts.

evidence.requirement: No arbitrary commands, shell, or forwarding
evidence.summary: The attempted command marker remained absent, stdin was stored instead, forwarding failed, PTY was disabled, and the forced-command policy persisted after reboot.
Both nodes report the same AlmaLinux 9.6 release and 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 kernel before and after changes.
Healthy baseline boot ID a0d04bc6…, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID aebd7945…, active SSH, retained data, persistent restrictions, and successful fresh ingestion were demonstrated.
Healthy baseline boot ID ea4e3fbd…, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID fcaf1466…, recovered uploader key/configuration, and successful end-to-end ingestion were demonstrated.
